summary: Wilkes-Barre postmaster under Theodore Roosevelt and Taft and owner of the Sunday Independent; brother of Catherine Heffernan Pringle and John's 2nd-great-grand-uncle.
bio:
Thomas F. Heffernan was born on 10 March 1871, a brother of John's 2nd-great-grandmother Catherine E. Heffernan Pringle. He was educated at Wyoming Seminary, taught for three years in the Plymouth schools and then spent thirteen years as a reporter on the Wilkes-Barre Record. He was assistant county treasurer in 1901, chairman of the Luzerne County Republican Committee through the campaigns of 1903, 1904 and 1905, and president of the Press Club of Wilkes-Barre; a portrait of him appeared in Prominent Men of Wilkes-Barre and Vicinity in 1906.

In 1907 President Theodore Roosevelt appointed him postmaster of Wilkes-Barre, and President Taft reappointed him in 1911; he held the office for eight years and eleven months, until 1916. Meanwhile he had become a newspaper owner. With John A. Hourigan he turned the Morning News into the Evening News in 1909, and in 1913 he bought the Sunday Independent from John J. Maloney, incorporating it in 1915 with his brothers John V. and George P. Heffernan. As "the only Sunday journal" in the valley, the paper had a net circulation of 18,777 an issue in 1926 and about 22,000 by 1929. A Republican, he was also a trustee of Mercy Hospital and a director of the Wilkes-Barre Deposit & Savings Bank.

On 20 June 1900, at Mauch Chunk, he married Louise Easen, who was born in England; their only son, Thomas E. Heffernan, was born in 1902. Thomas died at Wilkes-Barre on 28 February 1951, or the 27th by one record, and was buried at Fern Knoll Cemetery, Dallas. His family still ran the Sunday Independent in the 1960s and 1970s, carrying it through the Wilkes-Barre newspaper strikes of 1972 and 1978–79.
notable: Postmaster of Wilkes-Barre 1907-16; owner of the Sunday Independent from 1913

researchNotes:
Thomas F. Heffernan (10 Mar 1871 - 28 Feb 1951) taught three years in the Plymouth schools, then worked 13 years at the Wilkes-Barre Record. He was assistant county treasurer in 1901 and postmaster of Wilkes-Barre 1907-16 (8 years 11 months), appointed by Theodore Roosevelt in 1907 and reappointed by Taft in 1911. With John A. Hourigan he turned the Morning News into the Evening News (1909). In 1913 he bought the Sunday Independent from John J. Maloney and incorporated it in 1915 with his brothers John V. and George P.; net circulation was 18,777 per issue in 1926 and about 22,000 by 1929, as 'the only Sunday journal' in the valley. Republican; trustee of Mercy Hospital; director of the Wilkes-Barre Deposit & Savings Bank. He married Louise Easen (b. England) at Mauch Chunk in 1900; one son, Thomas E. (b. 1902). Buried Fern Knoll Cemetery, Dallas. The family still ran the Sunday Independent in the 1960s-70s, including through the 1972 and 1978-79 Wilkes-Barre newspaper strikes. The paper's 1913-1958 run is digitized by the Osterhout Free Library on POWER Library. Dwyer credits a portrait of him to Prominent Men, Wilkes-Barre (1906).

A 1906 portrait of Thomas F. Heffernan appears as no. 1114 in Prominent Men of Wilkes-Barre and Vicinity ([R4-S2]). Its caption-key adds facts not in the earlier sketches: educated at Wyoming Seminary, married Louise Easen on 20 June 1900, chairman of the Luzerne County Republican Committee during the 1903, 1904 and 1905 campaigns, and president of the Press Club of Wilkes-Barre. That was the year before Roosevelt made him postmaster. The state death index lists him on 28 Feb 1951, Wilkes-Barre, file 14086 ([R4-S1]). FamilySearch gives 27 Feb 1951 and burial at Fern Knoll, Dallas Twp ([R4-S3]).
